question: What does the code editor's full-screen button do, what is Learn More, and when do code and embed blocks change rows?
page: a new blank page, nothing saved, a 1600 by 1000 window

button.label: Expand
button.note: Bottom right of the code editor in a code block's Content tab, 4px from each edge. Embed data has none.

expand.closing: Close, Escape and a click on the scrim all close it. The Edit panel is still there after each.
expand.typing: The block does not change while the view is open. Code typed there reaches the block and the panel's editor on closing.
expand.source: Display Source Code on or off in the view leaves the block as it is while the view is open.
expand.undo: After code typed in the view and Close, one Undo brings the old code back on the block and in the panel.

learnMore.note: It ends the note Paste the URL of the item..., in that text. Its target is a help page of the host, not read here.

rows.note: Each step replaces the code. Rows read after each step; the embed's steps pass through empty, as a person selecting and deleting does.

rows.rule: Inferred from these readings, it holds for all of them: a block that its content outgrows takes just the rows the content needs; when the content needs fewer rows, the block gives up that many and keeps the rest. Empty code changes nothing. An embed stays at 2 rows or more.

notMeasured: what Mode does in the full-screen view: the control was located, not pressed
whether Display Source Code set in the view reaches the block on closing: on then off left it as it was
rows after a pull with the mouse, or on the phone
